A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VSFA research. All pages, tables, figures, and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched reliably despite reflow and the addition of Appendix C.8 and Appendices D–G.

before.justification: v1 reports original safety and capability evaluations, modality ablations, and SAE activation-steering experiments in Tables 1–2 and Figures 2–3.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds original teacher comparisons, visual-style ablations, reasoning-benchmark evaluations, and additional model-family results in Tables 9–12.

M1.justification: The proposed pipeline remains GPT-4o-mini-assisted threat-image and neutral-VQA construction followed by LoRA tuning with the vision encoder frozen. The new teacher comparison justifies the existing teacher choice; it does not replace the proposed method or change its training procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix F adds MMLU's 57-subject text evaluation and MMMU's 30-subject multimodal academic reasoning evaluation, substantially broadening capability coverage beyond MM-Vet. The original safety benchmarks and training-domain coverage remain. Additional model sizes and smaller training sets are configuration changes rather than new task coverage.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain AdaShield, VLGuard, and their original undefended controls. New Table 9 adds GPT-5, Claude 4.5 Sonnet, and Gemini-3-pro teacher variants as comparators against the GPT-4o-mini-based pipeline. This expands component-level comparisons without adding a new defense baseline to the original experiments.

E3.justification: New experimental designs use 60 images and approximately 360 QA pairs per teacher, separate 50-image training sets for each visual style, and 60-image tuning of Gemma 3 IT 4B and Llama 3.2 Vision 11B. Appendix F adds before/after reasoning evaluations. The original main-experiment training settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices D and E introduce substantial analyses of teacher choice and sensitivity to all 12 visual styles. Appendix G tests generalization across additional architectures and sizes. The original modality ablation and SAE steering analysis remain; Appendix C.8 adds literature-based discussion rather than new cross-model SAE experiments.

E5.justification: Appendix E newly summarizes performance dispersion across style conditions with mean ASR 12.5% and reported standard deviation 0.74 percentage points. This is cross-style variability, not repeated-seed uncertainty. No confidence intervals or significance tests are added, and the multiple-seed evidence in Appendix C.8 is attributed to another work.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figures 2–3 retain their results. New Table 9 reports teacher-dependent ASRs of 12.0%, 22.2%, 28.8%, and 22.8%; Table 10 reports style-specific ASRs of 11.2–13.7%. Table 11 adds MMLU 68.52% to 68.13% and MMMU 50.56% to 50.11%. Table 12 adds Gemma ASR 37.0% to 7.2% and Llama ASR 49.8% to 17.6%. These are newly reported experiments, not improvements over v1 under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: The self-fulfilling hypothesis and SAE identification and steering reasoning are retained. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and v2's new generalization arguments are empirical interpretations rather than new mathematical results.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same central claims: label-free visual self-fulfilling alignment, reduced attack success, more constructive responses, less over-refusal, and preserved general capabilities. The additional experiments support these claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive explanations linking teacher effectiveness to concrete prompts and concise answers, style robustness to semantic rather than visual appearance, and model-family results to broadly shared persona mechanisms and data efficiency. Appendix C.8 extends the mechanistic interpretation using cited research. The original limitations remain, including the now-outdated restriction to four 7B–8B models.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-repository link in the abstract and documents controls and sample sizes for the new teacher, style, and model-family experiments. The original generation prompts, filtering rules, LoRA settings, hardware, software versions, and training-time disclosures remain unchanged. Repository contents cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds Arditi and Chen's persona-feature work and Gu et al.'s MiniLLM to support new interpretations, alongside new benchmark, model, and steering-related citations. Cocchi et al. and Jain et al. are removed. The central positioning against explicit safety supervision remains; numerous other reference edits are bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section organization are retained. v2 adds a teacher-choice paragraph, appendix sections and cross-references, acknowledgments, and equal-contribution information, with limited grammatical editing. Existing Appendices A–C.7 are essentially unchanged rather than substantially rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 adds four compact result tables, Tables 9–12. The existing figures retain their designs and contents. Main Tables 1–2 are relocated and their captions move below the tables; Table 2 now shares a page with Figure 2. The overall two-column layout remains.

improvement.justification: The teacher and style studies provide useful evidence for previously untested design choices, while direct MMLU/MMMU before/after comparisons strengthen capability-preservation evidence and additional families broaden applicability. These improve empirical support, but the new ablations remain limited to one model and attack benchmark, repeated-run uncertainty is absent, and cross-family mechanistic explanations remain inferential. The unchanged limitations also conflict with the expanded model evaluation.
